Finite forests alone give compatible classes. To obtain actual continuous representations, we use the following explicit coefficient and admissibility data. They also delimit the meaning of completion in the next theorem.

Fix a topological group \(\Gamma\), a finite matrix index set \(D\), and a set \(\Lambda\) of coefficient indices. For each \(\lambda\), let \(\OO_\lambda\) be a commutative ring, complete and separated for a finitely generated ideal \(I_\lambda\), with finite residue ring \(\OO_\lambda/I_\lambda\). Give \(\OO_\lambda\) its ideal adic topology and every quotient its discrete topology. Let
\[
i_\lambda:\OO_\lambda\longrightarrow K_\lambda,
\qquad e_\lambda:L\longrightarrow K_\lambda
\]
be supplied ring homomorphisms, where \(L\) and \(K_\lambda\) are fields, \(K_\lambda\) has a declared topology, and \(i_\lambda\) is continuous.

For every positive integer \(n\), let \(X_{\lambda,n}\) be a finite nonempty set of conjugacy classes of actual continuous representations
\[
\Gamma\longrightarrow\GL_D(\OO_\lambda/I_\lambda^n).
\]
Conjugacy means change of basis by an invertible matrix over that quotient. Assume reduction preserves these sets and that \(X_{\lambda,1}\) consists of the declared residual class. Each admissible class must have a continuous representative. The auxiliary level zero is the unique class over the trivial quotient and imposes no extra occupancy hypothesis.

Choose elements \(\gamma_v\in\Gamma\) on a sample set \(\Omega\), with declared good subsets \(\Omega_\lambda\subseteq\Omega\). In the arithmetic application these are the chosen Frobenius elements at the permitted places. For each \(v\in\Omega_\lambda\), supply an integral polynomial \(P_{\lambda,v}\in\OO_\lambda[X]\) such that
\[
i_\lambda(P_{\lambda,v})=e_\lambda(P_v)\quad\text{in }K_\lambda[X].
\]
Here and below a ring homomorphism applied to a polynomial acts on its coefficients. Assume every representative of every class in \(X_{\lambda,n}\) has characteristic polynomial \(P_{\lambda,v}\bmod I_\lambda^n\) at \(\gamma_v\). Also supply a subgroup \(H_\lambda\leq\Gamma\) on which all these finite representations are trivial. This is an inertia condition when \(H_\lambda\) is the specified inertia subgroup.

Finally, put
\[
B_\lambda=\OO_\lambda[x_{g,a,b}:g\in\Gamma,\ a,b\in D].
\]
For each declared local condition index \(u\), supply an ideal \(J_{\lambda,u}\subseteq B_\lambda\). Evaluation at a representation sends \(x_{g,a,b}\) to its \((a,b)\) matrix entry at \(g\). Assume that evaluation at every admissible finite representative kills \(J_{\lambda,u}\), with polynomial coefficients reduced modulo \(I_\lambda^n\). For this class based theorem, the equations must hold in every admissible frame. A condition imposed only in one chosen frame needs a separate compatible frame argument. No arbitrary arithmetic condition is identified with such an ideal without a separate argument.

\begin{theorem}[Conditional simultaneous companion completion]\label{thm:simultaneous_companion_completion}
Under the coefficient and finite admissibility hypotheses above, one can choose continuous representations
\[
\rho_\lambda:\Gamma\longrightarrow\GL_D(\OO_\lambda)
\qquad(\lambda\in\Lambda)
\]
whose reduction class belongs to \(X_{\lambda,n}\) for every positive \(n\). They retain the declared residual class. After applying \(i_\lambda\), they are continuous, trivial on \(H_\lambda\), and satisfy
\[
\det\!\left(X- i_\lambda(\rho_\lambda(\gamma_v))\right)
=e_\lambda(P_v),\qquad v\in\Omega_\lambda.
\]
Their integral evaluation points factor through every actual quotient \(B_\lambda/J_{\lambda,u}\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The finitely generated ideal and finite residue ring give finite coefficient quotients at every precision. An individual conjugacy class has finitely many frames because the group of invertible basis matrices over each quotient is finite. Thus the finitely many admissible classes give a finite nonempty set of actual continuous representations at each positive level. Continuity is invariant under conjugation. Reduction gives total maps between these sets. Compactness, as in \cref{thm:companion_branch_criterion}, selects strictly compatible representatives. This step neither assumes transition surjectivity nor lifts a prescribed conjugating matrix.

Completeness and separatedness identify \(\GL_D(\OO_\lambda)\) with the compatible inverse limit of the quotient matrix groups. Lift entries and inverse entries to construct this identification. The two reduction and reconstruction identities hold entrywise. Finite quotient continuity implies continuity for the ideal adic topology, including the matrix inverse, so the reconstructed representation is continuous.

Each coefficient of its characteristic polynomial agrees with the prescribed integral coefficient modulo every positive power of \(I_\lambda\). Separatedness gives equality of the full polynomials. The same argument applied to the matrix entries of \(\rho_\lambda(g)-1\) gives triviality on \(H_\lambda\). Continuous coefficient change and the matching equations for \(P_{\lambda,v}\) give the asserted common spine over the local fields.

For \(p\in J_{\lambda,u}\), evaluation commutes with reduction. Its value is zero modulo every positive power of \(I_\lambda\), hence is zero integrally by separatedness. Therefore the evaluation homomorphism kills the whole ideal and factors uniquely through \(B_\lambda/J_{\lambda,u}\). Choose a realization for each \(\lambda\).
\end{proof}

The quotient conclusion is a proved effectivity statement for the declared polynomial relations. For local conditions presented by continuous maps from represented local rings, \cref{cor:simultaneous_local} also accounts for the closed ideal generated by their defining ideals. Neither statement constructs a deformation ring for a condition that has not been shown representable. Hodge conditions, Weil--Deligne conditions, integral lifts of arbitrary Frobenius polynomials, and the finite occupancy hypotheses still require their own arithmetic inputs. The theorem retains a residual conjugacy class, not a prescribed residual matrix frame, and asserts no uniqueness up to integral conjugacy.

\section*{Lean verification and revision scope}

The accompanying Lean release 0.15.0 contains 546 theorem declarations written for Paper XII, including supporting lemmas and interface results. A further 81 theorem declarations are reused unchanged from Paper X and counted separately. All 71 project modules were rebuilt with Lean 4.34.0-rc2 and warnings treated as errors. The transitive axiom audit covers 934 named declarations and allows only the standard axioms \texttt{propext}, \texttt{Classical.choice}, and \texttt{Quot.sound}. Both deliberately invalid proof controls were rejected. These checks validate the formal statements under their explicit hypotheses, not every prose claim or external arithmetic input in this article.

Of the 49 internal numbered claims in this revised manuscript, 43 have complete mapped Lean statements, one is partial, and 5 are not yet fully checked. The partial claim is \cref{thm:rt_support_transport}, whose intrinsic Fitting ideal transport clause remains open in the formalization. The eight stated external arithmetic facts are excluded from these counts. Formal proof coverage is recorded claim by claim in the accompanying roadmap.

The new checks for \cref{prop:group_algebra_transfer,thm:coinvariant_recovery,cor:dyadic_coinvariant_recovery} include actual group algebra transfer and augmentation. Coinvariant recovery uses the quotient by all balancing relations, with its universal property proved. In the commutative case, this construction is identified with the ordinary tensor product. The augmentation relations generate exactly the augmentation ideal acting on the module. Applying augmentation to the coordinates of a supplied free basis gives a coefficient basis with the same index set. The right module argument applies to arbitrary groups, including nonabelian two groups, and includes rank zero.

The new checks for \cref{thm:residual_augmentation_algebra,cor:no_residual_character_splitting,cor:rank_trace_detection,prop:dyadic_sign_projectors} construct the full multivariable truncated polynomial algebra isomorphism and identify its augmentation generators. The residual group algebra is local for abelian \(p\) groups in characteristic \(p\). For each supplied Hecke idempotent, the trace is the image dimension cast into the coefficient field; occupancy is equivalent to positive rank and, in characteristic zero, nonzero trace. The dyadic calculation gives the two rational sign projectors, proves that neither lies in the integral group algebra, and identifies the residual algebra with \(\FF_2[X]/(X^2)\).

Corollary~\ref{cor:no_residual_character_splitting} is now checked for every finite \(p\) group, including nonabelian groups, over every field of characteristic \(p\). The proof uses a finite prime field orbit span and a nonzero fixed vector. The original unrestricted statement is restored, and the earlier explicit abelian restriction is no longer needed.

The checks for \cref{prop:quotient_erases_component,thm:canonical_hecke_packets,cor:simultaneous_generalized_eigenspaces} now include the actual formal power series quotient and the canonical Hecke packet maps. In the node \(k[[x,y]]/(xy)\), quotienting by \((x)\) gives \(k[[y]]\), with support \(V(x)\); Lean verifies both irreducible components and the exclusion of the generic point \((y)\). The components can still meet, so this is not a claim that their supports are disjoint.

For the Hecke results, the canonical ring decomposition in \cref{fact:artin_decomposition} remains a declared external input. Its coordinates are the actual localization maps. The module direct sum, the packet identification with the localized module, and the formula \(v\mapsto v/1\) are constructed in Lean. Nilpotence in the selected Artin local factor, together with invertibility of a generator on each other factor, gives a single positive exponent for the simultaneous generalized eigenspace. The result includes the explicit generators \(T_i-\lambda_i\), agrees with the packet used in the trace theorem, and does not assume semisimplicity.

The revised five gate statement in \cref{thm:five_gate_completion} is now checked for both ordinary and derived carriers and for a general support comparison. The comparison is an actual inclusion of subsets of prime spectra, and scalar extension is proved to satisfy it. The coefficient quotient and ordinary or derived control maps yield finite level support; that conclusion is not supplied as a separate patching assumption. The specialized tensor module or derived cohomology supplies an actual nonzero eigenvector. The declared realization theorem is applied to this particular eigensystem, and the resulting representation comparison is an actual invertible linear intertwiner. The system conclusion uses the family attached to the very same automorphic object, with distinguished member identities and a common algebraic polynomial spine.

The original comparison wording did not explicitly supply a compatible Hecke point over the fixed coefficient field. Support preservation alone is insufficient: extension from \(\mathbb Q\) to \(\mathbb Q(i)\) preserves full support, but there is no ring map \(\mathbb Q(i)\to\mathbb Q\) extending the identity. The revision therefore states \(y\circ f=x\) and exposes the arithmetic comparison and existing-family inputs. Residual occupancy, representability and the applicable patching theorem remain supplied arithmetic provenance. The original full statement remains partial. The remaining unchecked revised claims concern completed tensor quotients and intrinsic Fitting ideals, including the still partial Fitting transport clause.

The derived realization checks cover the revised \cref{thm:derived_pointwise_realization,thm:derived_conditional_completion}. They prove vanishing outside the bounds of an actual finite projective model and construct a nonzero cohomology vector inside those bounds. The Hecke action is induced from multiplication on the original cochain model, carried through scalar extension and derived localization, and proved to act by the specialized character on actual cohomology. The conditional arithmetic step gives an actual invertible linear intertwiner from the declared realization input and common Frobenius polynomials.

The original formulation of \cref{thm:derived_pointwise_realization} did not ensure that the surviving degree lies in the classicality range. A complex concentrated in degree one has full support over a field, while a classicality condition restricted to degree zero says nothing about its nonzero fiber. The revision requires the declared range to contain the model interval. The conditional conclusion of \cref{thm:derived_conditional_completion} retains applicability at the selected eigensystem itself. Both statements now expose the topology, continuity, semisimplification, and common polynomial inputs needed for the representation comparison. Their original unconditional cohomological conclusions are checked, but their original complete statements remain partial. The general support comparison and compatible-point formulation is now checked in the revised \cref{thm:five_gate_completion}, as described above.

The derived support checks prove \cref{thm:derived_quotient_support,thm:derived_support_descent,cor:derived_degree_survives} as originally stated. Perfect complexes are actual derived category objects equipped with bounded finite projective models and derived isomorphisms to those models. Scalar extension is constructed on cochain complexes. Its associativity, preservation of homotopy equivalences, and independence under actual derived isomorphisms are checked. The quotient support formula uses the actual map of spectra and its image \(V(I)\). Every field valued point factors through the residue field at its kernel, and faithful flatness of field extensions preserves and reflects acyclicity. The surviving integer degree is expressed using the actual derived cohomology functor, with a corresponding witness in the specialized cochain model. These proofs do not require the external cohomological support description in \cref{fact:derived_support_cohomology}. The external classicality theorems remain supplied arithmetic inputs; the conditional derived realization argument is checked as described above.

The adequacy checks prove \cref{thm:s3_adequacy} as originally stated. They construct the faithful standard representation from the actual permutation module, prove irreducibility after extension to the algebraic closure, and split every group element's characteristic polynomial over \(\FF_7\). The trace zero adjoint is the kernel of matrix trace with its conjugation action, and its sign plus standard decomposition is an actual equivariant linear isomorphism. The averaging proof is connected to Mathlib's actual first group cohomology, while the invariant calculation gives actual degree zero vanishing. Canonical projectors are identified with generalized eigenspace projectors for every positive exponent. Their trace pairings detect every nonzero endomorphism and hence every irreducible adjoint submodule. The two printed constituent witnesses and their traces are checked exactly. The adequacy definition remains a cited convention; no external adequacy theorem is assumed in this finite certificate.

The realization checks cover \cref{thm:pointwise_galois_realization,cor:full_support_pointwise_automorphy,thm:one_member_propagation,thm:ordinary_conditional_completion,thm:system_completion}. Characteristic polynomial coefficients are continuous by the principal minor formula. Equality on the declared Frobenius conjugacy classes therefore extends to the whole Galois group. The finite dimensional algebra input is explicit: a supplied semisimple representative preserves every characteristic polynomial, and a general Brauer Nesbitt theorem identifies semisimple representations with equal polynomials. Lean proves independence of this representative and the irreducible conclusion. Construction of semisimplification, the general Brauer Nesbitt theorem, and arithmetic Chebotarev density remain external inputs.

The ordinary completion argument derives finite generation, full finite level support, and an actual nonzero Hecke tensor fiber from the patched support and control isomorphisms. The declared classicality input then supplies the occurring automorphic object and its attached representation. Both existing compatible systems, with their common polynomial spine, are retained as hypotheses in the propagation results. These results do not construct missing companions or an attached compatible system.

The pointwise realization and ordinary completion statements now explicitly require Hausdorff coefficient topology and continuity of the compared representations, including the universal specialization. The corresponding locus statement is restricted to such points. These three revised claims are counted as complete; their original wording remains partial. This clarification also makes the coefficient topology in \cref{fact:chebotarev_brauer_nesbitt} explicit without claiming a new proof of that external arithmetic fact.

The earlier revision made two further substantive corrections. In \cref{cor:componentwise_occupancy}, every irreducible component is contained in the full support. The previous sentence reversed that containment. In \cref{thm:simultaneous_companion_completion}, the coefficient, continuity, integrality, class finiteness, and quotient condition hypotheses are now explicit. Finite forests by themselves establish branches, not all arithmetic effectivity assertions. Corollary~\ref{cor:simultaneous_local} now gives the closed kernel argument and the continuity and uniqueness of its factors.

The original manuscript and its literal claim records are preserved with the release. In that original census, 35 claims are fully checked, eight are partial, and 6 are not checked as written. The corrected \cref{cor:componentwise_occupancy} and restricted \cref{thm:simultaneous_companion_completion} are counted as proved only for their revised statements. The original unrestricted completion wording is not retrospectively marked proved. Source hashes, the exact amendments, compiler logs, and an authoring-assistant mathematical self-review accompany the code.

\begin{standardfact}[Chebotarev and Brauer Nesbitt identification]\label{fact:chebotarev_brauer_nesbitt}
Let \(E'\) be a characteristic zero field. Let
\[
\rho_1,\rho_2:G_{F,S}\longrightarrow\GL_n(E')
\]
be continuous semisimple representations. If their characteristic polynomials agree at every Frobenius element outside a density zero exceptional set, then
\[
\boxed{\rho_1\cong\rho_2.}
\]
This follows from Chebotarev density and the Brauer Nesbitt theorem
\cite{BrauerNesbitt1941,Neukirch1999}.
\end{standardfact}
edits.after:

\begin{theorem}[Pointwise Galois realization]\label{thm:pointwise_galois_realization}
Assume the following data.
\begin{enumerate}
\item A represented deformation ring \(R\) with universal representation
\[
\rho_R:G_{F,S}\longrightarrow\GL_n(R).
\]
\item An isomorphism \(R\cong\TT\).
\item An automorphic Hecke datum \((\TT,H,(P_v))\).
\item A characteristic zero point \(x:R\to E'\) lying in \(\Supp_R(H)\).
\item A classical automorphic representation \(\pi_x\) occurring in the fiber \(H_x\), together with a semisimple attached representation
\[
\rho_{\pi_x}:G_{F,S}\longrightarrow\GL_n(E')
\]
whose unramified characteristic polynomial is \(x(P_v(X))\).
\item Equality
\[
\det\left(X-\rho_x(\Frob_v)\right)=x(P_v(X))
\]
for \(\rho_x=x\circ\rho_R\) at every unramified place in a Chebotarev dense set.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\[
\boxed{
\rho_x^{\mathrm{ss}}
\cong
\rho_{\pi_x}.
}
\]
If \(\rho_x\) is irreducible, then \(\rho_x\cong\rho_{\pi_x}\).
\end{theorem}

The first assertion follows from locality in \cref{thm:residual_augmentation_algebra}. For the general finite \(p\) group assertion, let \(e\in k[G]\) be idempotent and write \(\epsilon:k[G]\to k\) for augmentation. Suppose \(\epsilon(e)=0\) and \(e\ne0\). The \(\FF_p\) span \(W\) of the left translates \(ge\) is a nonzero finite dimensional \(\FF_p\) vector space, stable under \(G\). Its cardinality is divisible by \(p\). The orbit counting formula implies that its fixed point set also has cardinality divisible by \(p\). Since zero is fixed, there is a nonzero fixed vector \(v\in W\).

A vector in the regular representation fixed by all left translations has constant coefficients. Consequently \(ve=\epsilon(e)v=0\). On the other hand, \(e^2=e\) implies \(we=w\) for every \(w\in W\), hence \(ve=v\), a contradiction. Thus every idempotent of augmentation zero is zero. Since \(\epsilon(e)^2=\epsilon(e)\) in the field \(k\), either \(\epsilon(e)=0\) or \(\epsilon(e)=1\); in the latter case apply the preceding argument to \(1-e\).

A semisimplification has the same characteristic polynomials as the original representation. The algebraic Brauer Nesbitt input in \cref{fact:chebotarev_brauer_nesbitt} thus gives \(\rho_x^{\mathrm{ss}}\cong\rho_{\pi_x}\). If \(\rho_x\) is irreducible, it is already semisimple.

(X-1)^2,\qquad (X-1)(X+1),\qquad (X-2)(X-4).
\]
Thus all eigenvalues already lie in \(\FF_7\).

A trace zero matrix fixed by conjugation by both \(s\) and \(t\) is zero, as follows by comparing its four entries. This proves \(H^0(S_3,\ad^0V)=0\). For any \(\FF_7[S_3]\) module \(M\) and one cocycle \(f\), put
\[
u=-6^{-1}\sum_{h\in S_3}f(h).
\]
Summing \(f(gh)=g f(h)+f(g)\) over \(h\) gives \(gu-u=f(g)\). Hence every one cocycle is a coboundary and \(H^1(S_3,M)=0\), giving both asserted first cohomology vanishings.

Write
\[
W(a,b,c)=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&-a\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
Z=W(2,3,4),\quad A=W(1,1,2),\quad B=W(1,5,6).
\]
The three coordinate columns have determinant \(3\ne0\). Under conjugation,
\[
sZ=-Z,\quad tZ=Z,\qquad
sA=-A,\quad sB=A+B,\quad tA=B,\quad tB=-A-B.
\]
Consequently \((z,(a,b))\mapsto zZ+aA+bB\) is an equivariant isomorphism from \(\operatorname{sgn}\oplus V\) to \(\ad^0V\).

The sign witness is \(W_{\mathrm{sgn}}=Z\), while
\(W_{\mathrm{std}}=W(6,4,3)=3A+3B\) belongs to the standard summand. The corresponding projectors and trace pairings are
\[
P_{t,2}=\begin{pmatrix}2&4\\3&6\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \Tr(P_{t,2}W_{\mathrm{sgn}})=3\ne0,
\]
\[
P_{s,1}=\begin{pmatrix}0&4\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \Tr(P_{s,1}W_{\mathrm{std}})=6\ne0.
\]
For an operator \(D\) with \((D-\alpha I)(D-\beta I)=0\) and \(\alpha\ne\beta\), the canonical projector is
\[
P_{D,\alpha}=(\alpha-\beta)^{-1}(D-\beta I).
\]
Its image equals \(\ker((D-\alpha I)^n)\) for every \(n\ge1\), and it kills \(\ker((D-\beta I)^n)\). This identifies the displayed matrices with the generalized eigenspace projectors required in the adequacy definition.

For detection on every irreducible submodule, one can check the stronger assertion that canonical projectors detect every nonzero matrix. In addition to the two projectors above, use
\[
P_{s,-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\0&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
P_{tst^{-1},1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\4&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The four trace pairings with these matrices have trivial common kernel in \(M_2(\FF_7)\), by row reduction. Every irreducible adjoint submodule contains a nonzero matrix, so some canonical projector has nonzero trace pairing on that submodule. This verifies the last adequacy clause and completes the certificate.

Scalar extension to a commutative \(R\) algebra \(S\) is computed degree by degree as \(S\otimes_RP\); the canonical symmetry of tensor products gives the displayed order \(C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S\). Let \(q\in\Spec(R/I)\), and let \(\frakp\) be its inverse image in \(R\). The composite point \(R\to R/I\to\kappa(q)\) has kernel \(\frakp\), so it factors through a field embedding \(\kappa(\frakp)\to\kappa(q)\). The ordinary tensor associator in every degree gives an isomorphism of complexes
\[

\cong\kappa(q)\otimes_RP
\cong\kappa(q)\otimes_{\kappa(\frakp)}
\bigl(\kappa(\frakp)\otimes_RP\bigr).
\]

The left hand complex is thus nonzero in the derived category exactly when the residue field fiber of \(C\) at \(\frakp\) is nonzero. This proves the support identity on corresponding primes. The image of \(\Spec(R/I)\to\Spec R\) is exactly \(V(I)\), giving the stated ambient spectrum equality, including the case \(I=R\).

\begin{theorem}[Derived pointwise realization]\label{thm:derived_pointwise_realization}
Let \(R\cong\TT\), and let \(C\) be a perfect automorphic Hecke complex with full derived support. For every characteristic zero point \(x:R\to E'\), there is an integer \(i\) such that
\[
H^i
\left(
C\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}\limits_{R,x}^{\mathbf L}}E'
\right)
\neq0.
\]
If every nonzero Hecke eigensystem in the declared cohomological range satisfies the required classicality and Galois realization theorem, then the specialization \(\rho_x\) is automorphic after semisimplification.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Derived pointwise realization]\label{thm:derived_pointwise_realization}
Let \(e:R\cong\TT\), and let \(C\) be a perfect automorphic Hecke complex with full derived support. Choose a bounded finite projective model for \(C\), supported in degrees \([a,b]\). For every characteristic zero point \(x:R\to E'\), write \(y=x\circ e^{-1}\). Then some integer \(i\in[a,b]\) has
\[
H^i\left(C\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}\limits_{\TT,y}^{\mathbf L}}E'\right)\neq0.
\]
Every \(t\in\TT\) acts on this cohomology through \(y(t)\).

For the realization conclusion, give \(E'\) a Hausdorff topological field structure. Supply a universal representation \(\rho_R\), a continuous specialization \(\rho_x=x\circ\rho_R\), and a semisimplification of \(\rho_x\). Suppose its characteristic polynomials on a Chebotarev dense set are \(y(P_v(X))\). Let the declared classicality range contain \([a,b]\). Assume that every nonzero Hecke eigensystem in that range is realized by a classical automorphic representation occurring in that degree, with a continuous semisimple attached representation whose characteristic polynomials on the same dense set are \(y(P_v(X))\). With the standard Chebotarev density and Brauer Nesbitt inputs of \cref{fact:chebotarev_brauer_nesbitt}, the specialization \(\rho_x\) is automorphic after semisimplification. If \(\rho_x\) is irreducible, it is itself isomorphic to the attached representation.
\end{theorem}

Full derived support gives a nonzero fiber at \(y\). Scalar extension of the chosen projective model preserves its degree bounds. Its cohomology therefore vanishes below \(a\) and above \(b\). Since vanishing in every degree is equivalent to being zero in the derived category, some degree \(i\in[a,b]\) has nonzero cohomology. Choose a nonzero vector in that cohomology module.

Multiplication by \(t\in\TT\) is a cochain endomorphism of the original model. In the scalar extension the tensor relation identifies this endomorphism with \(y(t)\) times the identity. Passing to the derived category and then to cohomology preserves this equality. Thus the chosen vector is a common Hecke eigenvector with character \(y\).

The interval inclusion puts this eigensystem in the declared classicality range. Apply the realization input to obtain an occurring automorphic representation and its continuous semisimple attached representation. Its Frobenius characteristic polynomials agree with those of \(\rho_x\) on the prescribed dense set. Continuity extends the equality to every group element. The supplied semisimplification preserves these polynomials, so the general Brauer Nesbitt input gives an invertible linear intertwiner. If \(\rho_x\) is irreducible, it is already semisimple and the same comparison applies directly.

Full support descends from the patched perfect complex by \cref{thm:derived_support_descent}. Scalar transport through \(e\), followed by the actual derived isomorphism with the automorphic Hecke complex, gives full support for \(C\). Its fiber at \(y\) is therefore nonzero. The bounded model and induced Hecke action argument in \cref{thm:derived_pointwise_realization} supplies a nonzero cohomology eigenvector in an integer degree within the model's bounds.

If realization applies to this eigensystem, it supplies the occurring automorphic object and a continuous semisimple attached representation with the declared Frobenius polynomials. The representation comparison in \cref{thm:derived_pointwise_realization} then identifies the supplied semisimplification of \(\rho_x\) with that attached representation. \begin{theorem}[Five gate formulation]\label{thm:five_gate_completion}
Fix a characteristic zero deformation point \(x:R\to E'\). Give \(E'\) a Hausdorff topological field structure. The conditional argument uses the following five gates.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Residual gate.} Residual occupancy in the declared automorphic carrier and representability of the chosen deformation problem are supplied arithmetic inputs. In particular, the deformation ring \(R\) and its universal representation \(\rho_R\) are available.
\item \textbf{Patching gate.} An applicable patching theorem supplies an ordinary finite module or a perfect complex with full patched support, together with the coefficient quotient and the module or derived control isomorphism. Write \(M\) for the resulting finite level carrier over \(R\).
\item \textbf{Comparison gate.} Let \(H\) be a finite ordinary Hecke module or a perfect Hecke complex over \(\TT\). Supply a ring map \(f:R\to\TT\) satisfying
\[
(f^*)^{-1}\bigl(\Supp_R(M)\bigr)\subseteq\Supp_{\TT}(H).
\]
Use ordinary or derived support according to the carrier. Actual scalar extension satisfies this inclusion, as does transport through a ring isomorphism with the corresponding carrier identification.
\item \textbf{Fiber gate.} Supply a Hecke point \(y:\TT\to E'\) with \(y\circ f=x\). Then the fiber of \(H\) at \(y\) is nonzero. It contains a nonzero Hecke eigenvector, in some integer cohomological degree in the derived case, with character \(y\).
\item \textbf{Realization gate.} The declared classicality theorem applies to the resulting eigensystem and supplies an occurring classical automorphic representation \(\pi\), with a continuous semisimple attached representation. Require the specialization \(\rho_x=x\circ\rho_R\) to be continuous and supply its semisimplification. On the same Chebotarev dense set, assume that the characteristic polynomials of both \(\rho_x\) and the attached representation are \(y(P_v(X))\). Retain the standard density and general Brauer Nesbitt inputs of \cref{fact:chebotarev_brauer_nesbitt}.
\end{enumerate}
Then \(\rho_x^{\mathrm{ss}}\) is isomorphic to the representation attached to \(\pi\). If \(\rho_x\) is irreducible, the same conclusion holds for \(\rho_x\) itself.

For propagation, suppose both a semisimple compatible family \(\{\rho_\lambda\}\) containing \(\rho_x\) and a family \(\{\rho_{\pi,\lambda}\}\) attached to this same \(\pi\) already exist. Require the distinguished members to be \(\rho_x\) and its attached representation, respectively. Assume the coefficient, continuity, density, semisimplification and common algebraic Frobenius spine hypotheses of \cref{thm:one_member_propagation}, with that spine agreeing with the specialized Hecke polynomials at the distinguished place. Then
\[
\rho_\lambda\cong\rho_{\pi,\lambda}^{\mathrm{ss}}
\qquad\text{for every }\lambda.
\]
\end{theorem}

The patching gate and \cref{thm:ordinary_support_descent,thm:derived_support_descent} give full support at finite level. The comparison gate transports support to the Hecke side. The fiber gate follows from \cref{thm:field_fiber_criterion} in the ordinary case and from derived support in the complex case. The realization gate gives automorphy by \cref{thm:pointwise_galois_realization,thm:derived_pointwise_realization}. The compatible system statement is \cref{thm:one_member_propagation}.
edits.after:
The residual and representability inputs specify the setting in which the supplied patching theorem applies. The formal deduction begins with its actual rings, carriers and comparison maps. In the ordinary branch, finite generation and full support at finite level follow from the coefficient quotient and module control isomorphism. In the derived branch, the derived control isomorphism gives a perfect finite level model, and \cref{thm:derived_support_descent} gives full support.

The comparison inclusion transports this full support to \(H\). More specifically, \(y\circ f=x\) identifies the contraction of \(\ker y\) with \(\ker x\), so support at the source point gives support at the Hecke point. In the ordinary case, \cref{thm:field_fiber_criterion} gives a nonzero actual tensor fiber. In the derived case, the support criterion gives a nonzero actual derived fiber and hence a nonzero cohomology vector. Its integer degree lies within the bounds of the chosen finite projective model. In both cases, multiplication on the original carrier induces the scalar \(y(t)\) on the specialized vector for every \(t\in\TT\).

Choose this nonzero eigensystem and apply the declared realization theorem to it. No realization statement in other degrees is needed. The two continuous representations have the same characteristic polynomials on the declared dense Frobenius conjugacy classes. Continuity extends their equality to the whole group. The supplied semisimplification preserves those polynomials, and the general Brauer Nesbitt input gives the required invertible linear intertwiner. The irreducible conclusion follows as in \cref{thm:pointwise_galois_realization}.

Finally, retain the same \(\pi\) in its attached family. The distinguished member identities connect both families to the pointwise construction, while the common algebraic spine gives the required Frobenius polynomials at every coefficient place. Apply \cref{thm:one_member_propagation} to these two existing families. The construction does not produce a missing companion or an attached compatible family.
